definitions.explanation: A thin, shimmering sphere of soapy water blown into the air, popular as a children's plaything. シャボン derives from the Portuguese word for soap.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧シャボン{玉|だま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飛|と}ばす→飛ばす：02373_tobasu⟧。

⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧シャボン{玉|だま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}って→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦ふわふわ→ふわふわ：05156_fuwafuwa⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{舞|ま}い{上|あ}がった→舞い上がる：06043_maiagaru⟧。
examples.english: In the park, soap bubbles floated up on the breeze.

examples.japanese: {誕生日会|たんじょうびかい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧シャボン{玉|だま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦{実演|じつえん}→実演：19793_jitsuen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大人気|だいにんき}→大人気：12205_daininki⟧だった。
examples.english: At the birthday party, the demonstration of making giant soap bubbles was a big hit with the children.

notes:
A children's toy of bubbles blown from soapy liquid. シャボン derives from Portuguese 'sabão' (soap), brought to Japan centuries ago.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- シャボン{玉|だま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飛|と}ばす→飛ばす：02373_tobasu⟧: to blow soap bubbles
- シャボン{玉|だま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{割|わ}れる→割れる：00907_wareru⟧: a soap bubble pops

USAGE:
Because the bubbles burst so easily, シャボン{玉|だま} is also a poetic image for something beautiful but fleeting, as in the well-known children's song of the same name.
